subject: How to export results from estimation summary

messages.author: a77cc0d4882ca89e
messages.subject: How to export results from estimation summary
parts:
Hi,
I calculated bird abundance of more than 500 study plots using line
transects. I have finished the Distance calculations and like to use
the results in Excel now. However, Distance provides the results in
a very inconvenient way. How can I export the results from the
estimation summary, without copy-pasting all 500 single positions? I
need the name of the study plot (e.g. "BB1") and the abundance (e.g.
N=3D16) only.
Each position looks like the following example:

Sample: 1. BB1
Half-normal/Cosine
D 0.12461 5.25 1480.00 0.11242
0.13811
N 16.000 5.25 1480.00 15.000
18.000



Thanks, Thomas

messages.author: 12f269733c6eb9a2
messages.subject: Re: How to export results from estimation summary
parts:
Thomas:

I can't tell exactly how you have structured your Distance project, but
from the snippet of output you have provided, it looks like your plots
are stored at the 'sample layer.'

If that is the case, then you ought to be able to have all of those
estimates shunted into a text file, and then you can import that text
file into Excel. Visit the Users Guide Chapter 8 that describes
Conventional Distance Sampling Analysis. There is a section there
entitled 'Saving CDS results to file.' That describes creating a
results detail and probably more useful, a results stats file. The full
details of the structure of this stats file is described in the appendix
MCDS engine reference.

Follow that route, and if you have difficulties, give a shout.
